steps.title: 200 generations instead of 100
steps.why:
n04's best network came from generation 98 of 100, so evolution was probably still improving when it stopped.
Same recipe as n04 with twice the generations, from a fresh start so the training time stays honest. Shows how
much faster the car gets for the extra training time.

steps.title: PPO Smart: the steady one
steps.why:
PPO 32 with a learning rate that eases off to zero over the run. Every PPO run so far slips back after its best lap
check (p15 seed 1 ended at 4/5); smaller and smaller updates should let it settle on a good driver instead of
wandering away from it. The lap-time bonus was not used: on the ladder it made PPO less reliable (p16), as it did
NEAT Smart. The schedule is sized for 8 hours (about 20M frames at PPO 32's pace on this laptop).
steps.outcome: The steady one, and the fastest Championship car that finishes every race track: 20.58 s on all five, 0.2 s quicker than NEAT 16 and almost never on the grass (0.2% of frames). The easing learning rate did what it was meant to: where PPO 32 fell apart after hour 2, PPO Smart got steadier, holding all five validation tracks in 59% of lap checks in its last hour against PPO 32's 0%. Its fastest checkpoint came at 5 h 21 min. The schedule was sized at 20M frames and finished after 6 h 25 min, under the 8 h budget. Its 4-minute checkpoint finishes 4 of 5 race tracks (34.3 s).

steps.title: NEAT 16: the proven recipe
steps.why:
The best NEAT recipe from the ladder (n05): 16 rays facing forward over ±120°, 2000-frame training episodes,
+1 fitness per frame a lap beats 1000 frames, population 100. Trained from scratch for 8 hours. (A first
run stopped at 3.5 h on a "no faster lap for 2 h" rule that a single lucky lap check fooled; it was continued to 8 h.)
steps.outcome: The steady one. Its fastest checkpoint came near the end of the 8 hours (generation 401) and finishes all five race tracks in 20.8 s on average, never touching the grass. Its quickest-to-finish checkpoint (13 min) is fragile: 3 of 5 race tracks.

steps.title: Baseline: NEAT run 1
steps.why:
Population 100, every genome drives the same 3 random tracks per generation, fitness = raw game score,
champion picked on 5 held-out tracks. Starts as a plain 40→3 network. Its output decoding applied tanh twice,
so gas was capped at 0.88 and the brake never released below 0.12: a car with the handbrake on.
steps.outcome: Finishes all five tracks without touching the grass, but slowly: gas capped at 0.88 and the brake always partly on. The reference everything else is measured against.
steps.note: Selected at generation 127 by validation score.

steps.title: 32 forward rays instead of 16
steps.why:
32 forward rays instead of 16. Same as p14 otherwise: does PPO use the finer view (the NEAT 32 car got faster laps with it)?
The PPO lab (scripts/ppo_lab.py, short 600k-frame runs on 3 seeds, validation tracks only) found that PPO deciding every frame never learns to finish, in any control mode. Recipe 'raw3_r4_g995' scored best (seed 0: best 5/5, final 2/5, seed 1: best 5/5, final 2/5, seed 2: best 5/5, final 5/5). This step trains it for 3M frames on two seeds, benchmarked like every other step.
steps.outcome: 5/5 on both seeds (22.1 s and 21.9 s), the only PPO step to finish every race track on both seeds. It takes longer to get there (55-65 min against p14's 13-34 min), but the finer view makes it steadier. This is the recipe for the PPO 32 and PPO Smart championship cars.

steps.title: 2000-frame training episodes
steps.why:
Training episodes stopped at 1000 frames (20 s), but n02 needs 19-28 s per lap, so on long tracks a lap was never
finished during training and finishing it was never rewarded. The benchmark allows 2000 frames. Here training
and validation get 2000 frames too. Cars that stop making progress are still cut off after 100 frames, so the extra
time is only spent on cars that keep driving. Everything else as n02.
steps.outcome: Finishes all five tracks about 1 s per lap faster than n02 (22.1 s vs 23.2 s), with a smaller network (4 hidden, 62 links) and almost no time on the grass. The longer episodes cost training time: 1 h 45 min instead of 47 min. The best generation was 98 of 100, so it was probably still improving.

steps.title: PPO 32: the finer view
steps.why:
PPO 16's recipe with 32 forward rays (p15), the only PPO step that finished all five race tracks on both seeds.
Trained from scratch for 8 hours.
steps.outcome: Fast but restless. It lapped all five validation tracks after 5 minutes; that checkpoint finishes 4 of 5 race tracks, slowly (32.1 s, misses track 21). Its fastest checkpoint, at 1 h 24 min, finishes all five race tracks in 22.9 s, with the quickest single laps of any PPO car (16.1 s on track 3) but 35.7 s on track 34. After that it drifted: by hour 7 it finished almost no validation tracks (0.2 of 5 on average). With 32 rays it trains at about 880 frames/s against PPO 16's 1300.

steps.title: PPO 16: the lab winner
steps.why:
The recipe the PPO lab found (p14): decide every 4 frames and hold the controls in between, plan further ahead
(gamma 0.995), rewards normalised, 16 rays facing forward over ±120°. On the ladder it finished 4 of 5 race tracks on
both seeds after 13–34 min. Trained from scratch for 8 hours.
steps.outcome: The quick learner. It lapped all five validation tracks after 5 minutes, sooner than any NEAT car, and that checkpoint finishes 4 of 5 race tracks (25.1 s; it misses track 34). Its fastest checkpoint came at 2 h 32 min and finishes all five race tracks in 23.1 s, 2.3 s slower than NEAT 16: its 20.1 s validation laps didn't fully carry over (track 11 took 28.3 s). The last 5 hours added nothing; it held all five validation tracks less and less often. Paused once at 4 h 41 min and resumed from its last checkpoint.

steps.title: 16 forward rays instead of 32 all around
steps.why:
The original lidar fans 32 rays over 324° centred on the car's right side: 13 point backwards and there is a
36° blind gap on the left. In n00 the forward rays (about ±45°) carried most of the signal, and the side and
back rays barely changed. Here: 16 rays over ±120° around the nose. Half the inputs, no blind spot, and a
smaller network to evolve. Everything else as n01.
steps.outcome: Finishes all five tracks with half the inputs and in 47 minutes, a fifth of n00's training time. Laps are slower than n00 (23.2 s vs 20.9 s): it runs wide onto the grass on tracks 21 and 55 and loses 4-5 s there. Training episodes stop at 1000 frames (20 s), so a lap that long never finished during training.

steps.title: NEAT 32: twice the rays
steps.why:
Same as NEAT 16 but with 32 forward rays over the same ±120°: twice the detail ahead, but twice the inputs to evolve
and a slower simulation. Do more rays make a faster car, or only a slower-to-train one?
steps.outcome: More rays bought speed, slowly: its fastest checkpoint (6 h 10 min) laps in 19.2 s with a 16.7 s best, but misses one race track. Twice the inputs took about four times the training of NEAT 16 to reach its best laps.

steps.title: A lap-time bonus
steps.why:
A lap-time bonus. Same as p14 plus +1 per frame a lap beats 1000 frames, the bonus the NEAT cars train with: does it make PPO faster without crashing?
The PPO lab (scripts/ppo_lab.py, short 600k-frame runs on 3 seeds, validation tracks only) found that PPO deciding every frame never learns to finish, in any control mode. Recipe 'raw3_r4_g995' scored best (seed 0: best 5/5, final 2/5, seed 1: best 5/5, final 2/5, seed 2: best 5/5, final 5/5). This step trains it for 3M frames on two seeds, benchmarked like every other step.
steps.outcome: Seed 0 4/5, seed 1 3/5. Seed 0 kept the same checkpoint as p14 (the bonus only pays for laps under 20 s, which it didn't drive yet at 13 min); later it held 5/5 on validation less often (7% of lap checks against 28%). As with NEAT Smart, the speed bonus makes the car less reliable, so the PPO cars train without it.

steps.title: PPO lab winner: raw3 controls, decide every 4 frames
steps.why: The PPO lab (scripts/ppo_lab.py, short 600k-frame runs on 3 seeds, validation tracks only) found that PPO deciding every frame never learns to finish, in any control mode. Recipe 'raw3_r4_g995' scored best (seed 0: best 5/5, final 2/5, seed 1: best 5/5, final 2/5, seed 2: best 5/5, final 5/5). This step trains it for 3M frames on two seeds, benchmarked like every other step.
steps.outcome: 4/5 on both seeds (21.7 s and 23.2 s mean laps), the first PPO step to finish most race tracks under the fair rules. The kept seed needed 13 minutes. Deciding every 4 frames cut an episode from 2000 to 500 decisions, so PPO could connect a steering choice with the tiles it earned; planning further ahead (gamma 0.995) then made it hold up on all three lab seeds.

steps.title: Check: control + 16 forward rays
steps.why:
Second check: the control recipe with only the 16 forward rays added. If p05 learns and this doesn't, the ray
change is what hurts PPO.
steps.outcome: The best PPO model yet: 3/5 tracks, 18.4 s mean lap, and 16.8 s on track 3, the fastest lap any model has driven. No grass on the tracks it finishes. Forward rays help PPO as much as NEAT: best evaluation 896 vs 558 for the control.

steps.title: Fixed controls + reward lap time
steps.why:
Same recipe as the baseline, but with the corrected output decoding (full gas, brake can release),
speciation on, and +1 fitness per frame a lap finishes under 1000 frames, so faster laps clearly win.
Fresh start, so the training time is honest.
steps.outcome: Faster where it finishes: 17.3 s on track 3, the quickest NEAT lap so far. But it takes corners at 55-60 and on tracks 21 and 34 it leaves the road and never finds its way back. Its fitness only saw 1000-frame episodes, so long tracks were never finished in training.

steps.title: NEAT Smart: every lesson at once
steps.why:
NEAT 16 plus three lessons from the ladder. (1) No compass inputs: cos/sin(heading) are useless on random tracks,
and in n00 evolution had already cut cos(heading) off. (2) Five tracks per generation instead of three, so a network
can't win by drawing easy tracks. (3) A stronger lap-time bonus (2 per frame) to push harder for speed.
steps.outcome: Two very different cars. After only 18 minutes it already finished all five race tracks (27 s laps), the best quickest-to-finish car. Its fastest checkpoint laps validation in 18.5 s and sets the quickest race laps of any car (16.4-16.6 s), but crashes out on 3 of 5 race tracks: the stronger speed bonus made it fast but fragile.

steps.title: Normalise the reward
steps.why:
Tile rewards (+3.7), the time penalty (-0.1 per frame) and the end of a lap sit on very different scales, which
makes PPO's value estimates jumpy. Here the reward is scaled by a running estimate of the return's spread
(VecNormalize, rewards only). Everything else as p10.
steps.outcome: Seed 0 0/5, seed 1 2/5 (17.5 and 18.3 s laps). The only one of p10-p13 that helped, but the policy still peaked after about 4 minutes and then got worse. The exploration noise never shrank (std about 0.8 all run).

steps.title: Calmer exploration (gSDE)
steps.why:
PPO starts with action noise of standard deviation 1.0 on a steering range of -1 to 1: early on the car can
hardly drive straight. Here the noise starts much smaller (log std -2) and is state-dependent and smooth over
4 frames (gSDE), as in the RL Zoo's CarRacing recipe. Everything else as p11.
steps.outcome: Seed 0 0/5, seed 1 1/5 (17.7 s), with 99-100% of the lap on three more tracks. Smoother driving, but no more finishes than p11.

steps.title: Baseline: PPO, stopped at its peak
steps.why:
Stable-Baselines3 PPO, two 256-unit layers, 4 parallel envs, stopped at 450k steps because longer runs
collapsed. It was trained while the traction input was stuck at 1.0, so the off-track penalty never fired
and the network never learned what grass is.
steps.outcome: Fast when it gets it right (18.1 s on track 55), but it spends a lot of time on the grass and runs out of time on four of the five tracks.
steps.note: Best evaluation at 400k steps. Off-track penalty inactive (traction bug).

steps.title: Control: p00's recipe, only the real traction input
steps.why:
First of three short checks to find what broke PPO. This is p00's recipe exactly (32 original rays, no stuck rule,
no grass penalty, 1000-frame episodes, constant learning rate). The only difference from p00 is that the traction
input now works, which can't be undone. If this learns, the traction fix is not the problem.
steps.outcome: It learns, unlike p01-p04: training reward reached about 465 with full-length episodes, so the traction fix is not what broke PPO. But only 1/5 finished (track 3, 24.2 s), and the kept checkpoint came early (125k steps). Its training time is slightly inflated: test runs shared the CPU while it trained.

steps.title: PPO under NEAT's rules
steps.why:
Until now PPO was not judged like NEAT. It trained on 1000-frame episodes (laps over 20 s never finished),
kept whichever checkpoint scored best on 3 random tracks, used 4 of the 8 CPU threads, and drove without
NEAT's action smoothing. Here it follows the shared rulebook: 2000-frame episodes, training tracks from the
same pool, the same lap check on the 5 validation tracks to choose the kept model, the same 0.1 smoothing,
and 8 parallel envs. Run with two seeds so luck shows. Otherwise p06's recipe.
steps.outcome: 0/5 on both seeds; no lap check ever finished a validation track. With 2000-frame episodes and the shared rules, p06's recipe learned little (training reward 100-220). Equal rules alone don't fix PPO: the recipe has to change too.

steps.title: No grass penalty: end the episode when stuck
steps.why:
p01 and p02 failed because the per-frame grass penalty (up to 3.75 per frame for 1500 frames) swamped the tile
rewards, and the policy learned to creep. Here there is no grass penalty at all. Instead, as in NEAT, an episode
ends after 100 frames without reaching a new tile, and the time penalty for the rest of the episode is charged,
so getting lost or parking never pays. Grass is then only bad because it leads nowhere. Everything else as p02.
steps.outcome: Better than p01/p02: it no longer creeps, driving at speed 28-36 and covering 32-60% of each track. But it spends 73-86% of the time on the grass and never finishes. Training reward rose early, then flattened at about 200; the kept checkpoint is from 100k of 1M steps. Several settings changed at once since the recipe that worked (p00), so the next step goes back to it.

steps.title: Check: control + stuck rule
steps.why:
Third check: the control recipe with only the stuck rule added (end the episode after 100 frames without a new
tile). If p05 learns and this doesn't, cutting episodes short is what hurts PPO: the car gets little practice
recovering from the grass.
steps.outcome: The culprit. With the stuck rule, episodes last about 350 frames instead of 1000, the car spends 82-92% of the time on grass and finishes nothing. Cutting a lost car off early means PPO never practises getting back on the road, and that recovery is what it needs to learn. The stuck rule is dropped for PPO.

steps.title: RL Zoo's PPO settings for CarRacing
steps.why:
The update settings known to work for PPO on CarRacing (RL Baselines3 Zoo): shorter rollouts (512 steps per env),
smaller batches (128), a lower learning rate (1e-4) easing off over the run, no entropy bonus, and one 256-unit
layer. Everything else as p12.
steps.outcome: 0/5 on both seeds (best lap check 1/5). Settings that work for PPO on CarRacing's pixels did not carry over to our compact state. The PPO lab came next: the problem turned out to be how often PPO decides, not its hyperparameters.

steps.title: 16 forward rays instead of 32 all around
steps.why:
Same sensor change as NEAT n02. In p00 the 9 rays within ±45° of the nose carried 48% of the policy's lidar
sensitivity, and the 15 backward rays still carried 32%: likely noise it reacts to. 16 rays over ±120° remove the
backward rays and the blind spot on the left, and simulate about 25% faster, so the same number of steps trains
in less time. Everything else as p01.
steps.outcome: Failed the same way as p01, so the sensor change could not show its effect. The reward has to be fixed first (next PPO step).

steps.title: Back to p00's recipe, plus forward rays and the stuck rule
steps.why:
p01-p03 never learned to drive, and each one changed several settings at once compared with p00, the only PPO run
that learned. Here p00's recipe is restored as it was: constant learning rate, no KL early stop, 1000-frame
episodes, no lap-time bonus, no grass penalty. Only three things differ from p00: the 16 forward rays, the stuck
rule from p03, and the real traction input (p00 only ever saw 1.0). If this learns, the lap-time bonus comes back
as its own step.

steps.title: Train longer, with the learning rate easing off
steps.why:
p06 was still noisy after 600k steps. Here it trains for 1.5M steps, with the learning rate decaying to zero over the
run so the policy settles instead of collapsing late (as p00's longer run did). Everything else as p06.
steps.outcome: Worse than p06: 0/5 tracks. Its evaluation reward never got above about 420 (p06 reached 896). Apart from the longer run, only the learning-rate schedule differs, and the two runs split apart within minutes: a single PPO run depends a lot on luck. This led to the fair-rules rework (p10), with two seeds for every PPO step from now on.

steps.title: Real traction + reward lap time
steps.why:
The fixed traction input with a mild off-track penalty (the strict 15 × 0.99 recipe taught the car to park),
learning-rate decay against the late collapse, and +1 reward per frame a lap finishes under 1000 frames.
steps.outcome: Failed. The off-track penalty (up to 3.75 per frame, and episodes don't end on grass) swamped the tile rewards: evaluation rewards of -2000 to -5000, and the policy learned to creep at walking pace. Training was fast (1M steps in 27 minutes) but learned nothing useful.

steps.title: Keep the checkpoint that laps best
steps.why:
PPO kept its checkpoint by the reward on 3 random tracks, and p05/p06 kept surprisingly early ones. Here every 25k
steps the policy drives the 5 validation tracks (the same check NEAT uses), and the checkpoint with the most finished
laps and the fastest mean lap is kept. Training is the same as p08.
steps.outcome: Training is identical to p08 (same seed), so it is the same weak policy: its best lap check finished 1 of 5 validation tracks, and 0/5 on the benchmark. Picking the checkpoint by laps can't rescue a policy that never learned to finish, but it is the fairer rule, so every step from p10 on uses it.

steps.title: Start unconnected: evolve which inputs to use
steps.why:
Every earlier NEAT run started with all inputs wired to all outputs, and evolution never fully cut a single ray.
Here every network starts with no connections at all, and only gains them by mutation, so inputs that don't
help are simply never wired in. The NEAT page then shows which rays evolution chose. Everything else as n02.
steps.outcome: Evolution wired up only 8 connections and 1 hidden node, the simplest driver yet, and it gets round 98-99% of three tracks. But it cuts across the grass, gets lost, and never crosses the finish line. Too simple, or 100 generations was not enough to grow.
